title: Polaris data governance POC - weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on security and data governance. Covered SSO test progress, audit log retention options, SOC 2 artifacts request, and clarification on data residency/retention TTL during pilot. Agreed to run an SSO test and to share SOC2 pack and retention config spreadsheet. Next step: schedule security deep dive and enable longer audit log retention for trial environment.
topics: Hosted vs private data handling during POC
action_items: Avery Chen - send SOC2 Type II summary and relevant audit evidence links - due 2026-02-18
Diego Ramos - enable 12-month audit log retention on the pilot tenant and share access instructions - due 2026-02-17
Maya Singh - provide sample retention policy and confirm legal requirements for data residency - due 2026-02-20
Samir Patel - run SSO SAML test on 2026-02-19 and report failures in Jira (ticket #PL-SSO-12) - due 2026-02-19
next_steps: Security deep dive meeting with infra and security teams (proposed 2026-02-19)
AE to share pilot cost breakdown and token-level logging sample
Customer to confirm if pilot data must remain in eu-west-1 or can span regions
Redwood to provision KMS test instance for encryption demo
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Start: 09:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Maya (Polaris Sec), Owen (Polaris Platform), Laura (Compliance), Samir (Data)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): weekly security POC; asked for SOC2; SSO test flapping; asked for longer logs retention; KMS questions; next deep dive.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy valentine's day, i guess, um, i'll kick us off. We want to focus today on the security items you flagged last week - SSO, audit logs, retention, and the SOC2 artifacts request. Diego will cover the audit log options.

[00:38] Maya: thanks, yeah quick context, we've got a raft of internal auditors asking if the pilot data is retained longer than the default 30 days, and they want to see proof that audit logs are write-once and exportable. Also SSO issues - last week's test had a timeout.

[01:15] Diego: right, so first on SSO, we reproduced the timeout-- looks like a metadata mismatch in the SAML response, maybe an audience URL problem. Priya and I can walk through the assertion mapping live.

[02:05] Owen: the metadata we used was generated from the Okta side; i did notice the entityId had an extra slash, but okta ui sometimes hides that. Samir set up the test account.

[02:42] Priya: just to be explicit, we have AE+SE on this one so if the SSO test still fails we'll escalate to engineering. Diego, any idea how long fix takes?

[03:10] Diego: small config fix, once we get the corrected metadata should be 1-2 hours of config/test, worst case tomorrow morning if you can't jump on now.

[03:48] Maya: good. Next on logs — we saw the dashboard clips but need raw audit trail. Can you confirm export formats and whether logs are tamper-evident?

[04:20] Diego: audit logs are available as JSONL exports. We sign them and store with immutability flags when you opt in. For the pilot tenant the default is 30 days but we can extend to 12 months for pilot by request. That will be written to your tenant and accessible from the console and via S3 export.

[05:05] Laura: are those exports encrypted at rest? Also where are they stored regionally?

[05:28] Diego: yes AES-256 at rest, and we can integrate with your KMS - bring-your-own-key test is possible in the private deployment. For hosted pilot we have a KMS proxy option, which gives you per-tenant envelope encryption. Regionally you can pin to eu-west-1.

[06:02] Samir: so to confirm, for this pilot, can we have data residency in eu-west-1 and 12 month retention? That aligns with our compliance asks.

[06:28] Avery: yes, we can pin the pilot tenant to eu-west-1. Diego will enable 12-month audit log retention. Note: there might be cost implications, we'll send a short cost delta.

[07:10] Maya: also the auditors asked for SOC2 Type II evidence. Can you share the report and the control mappings?

[07:34] Avery: absolutely. I'll share a redacted SOC2 Type II summary and a controls mapping doc. For production customers we do provide the SOC2 report under NDA; for pilots we typically share the summary and the SOC2 coverage matrix. If you need the full report we can route through legal.

[08:05] Laura: that's fine to start, but we'll want the mapping to our internal control numbers, i.e., which Redwood control maps to PR.IM-3 etc.

[08:30] Avery: got it — we'll include that mapping.

[09:02] Owen: one more on logs — how quick is the export in a forensic case? If we need to pull 6 months of logs for an incident, what's the lead time?

[09:25] Diego: the export runs on demand; for larger volumes it can take a few hours. We can pre-stage a forensic export job; for pilot we'll do ad-hoc but we'll test an export during the deep dive.

[10:00] Samir: what's the schema of the audit entries? Does it capture token-level metadata, model variant, request/response hashes?

[10:25] Diego: yes we capture request metadata (route, model version, token counts), auth principal, and a response-hash. We don't store full PII by default, but you can opt in to store full responses if you need that for debugging; that's typically not recommended for regulated data.

[11:00] Maya: important — our legal says no full-response retention unless encrypted and limited. We'll prefer metadata-only.

[11:18] Avery: that's the default, so you're fine. If later you need full-response retention we'll handle per your policy.

[11:45] Laura: about SSO again, last week the SAML test intermittently failed with a 502 proxy error, any ideas?

[12:10] Diego: that 502 looks like a transient proxy timeout between our auth gateway and the SSO provider. We added retry logic in the auth flow yesterday; Priya, have we run the smoke?

[12:35] Priya: we ran a quick smoke and saw improvement, but we still hit a flake when sending large SAML payloads. We'll reproduce in staging and push a fix.

[13:05] Owen: we'll set up a focused SSO run with our automation — Samir will capture logs and send to you.

[13:28] Samir: noted, i'll attach logs to the Jira ticket.

[13:50] Maya: regarding private deployment — if the POC goes well and we move to private, what does the onboarding timeline look like for an on-prem or VPC private control plane?

[14:15] Avery: typical for Redwood Private is 8-12 weeks for a full on-prem install with integration into KMS and your network, but smaller VPC-based private control planes can be quicker, around 3-5 weeks depending on approvals.

[14:50] Laura: are there additional compliance artifacts for private customers?

[15:06] Diego: private customers receive the standard SOC2 artifacts and we can provide more detailed network diagrams and runbooks. We also offer HSM integration where required.

[15:40] Maya: cost concern — any quick rule of thumb for the audit log retention delta cost? If we move from 30 days to 12 months, what's the expected increase?

[16:02] Avery: rough ballpark is X% of storage cost, we'll provide a concrete delta. Diego will run an estimate and provide numbers per TB.

[16:30] Owen: for our pilot scale (about 5M tokens/week) what's the performance you saw in the last benchmark? latency numbers?

[16:52] Diego: in your initial run we saw p95 around 220ms on hosted with default batching. On dedicated configuration p95 dropped to ~140ms. These were on smaller context windows; we'll share the benchmark sheet.

[17:20] Samir: great, we need that benchmark sheet tied to model version and quantization level.

[17:45] Diego: noted. I'll include model flavor (redwood-1-small) and quantization notes.

[18:10] Maya: one more compliance ask — we need an audit trail of access to the admin console. Can Redwood provide user-level admin audit trails?

[18:30] Diego: yes, admin actions are logged separately and we can include change diffs for config changes. Those logs can also be exported with the audit logs.

[19:00] Laura: excellent. Any limitations on RBAC? We want role separation between devs and sec folk.

[19:18] Diego: RBAC supports granular roles (viewer, operator, admin, billing). We can do custom roles for enterprise.

[19:45] Avery: earlier Maya mentioned auditors wanting write-once storage. For the pilot we'll enable immutability flags on the bucket and provide the export.

[20:12] Maya: will that be enough to satisfy the evidence request for the auditors? They want chain-of-custody notes.

[20:30] Avery: we'll provide a short chain-of-custody note explaining retention and immutability for the exported logs; legal will sign the blurb under NDA if needed.

[21:05] Owen: timeline check — if Diego flips audit retention to 12 months today, and Avery shares SOC2 summary by Thursday, can we do the security deep dive on Thursday or Friday?

[21:30] Priya: i can propose times; looks like Thursday morning UTC works for us.

[21:58] Samir: Thurs 10:00 UTC is good from our side.

[22:15] Avery: perfect, we'll set it, anticipate engineering and network folks to join.

[22:40] Maya: any final open items? I want to confirm storage encryption with BYOK for the pilot. We've heard 'KMS proxy' but need steps.

[23:05] Diego: steps are: you provide a public key or KMS ARN, we configure tenant envelope encryption, then run a key rotation test. For the hosted pilot it's a proxy mode; for private you'll use real KMS integration. We'll document the steps and share a runbook.

[23:45] Laura: please add the runbook to the ticket.

[24:10] Avery: action summary — I'll send SOC2 summary, Diego enables 12-month logs and shares export instructions, Samir runs SSO automation test on Thursday, Priya will schedule the deep dive.

[24:45] Diego: one more note — when we enable longer retention we will tag the tenant "pilot-extended-retention" so billing is tracked separately.

[25:10] Owen: that's fine. Also can you add token-level cost logging so we can budget?

[25:30] Avery: yes we'll provide token-level logging sample and a cost estimate.

[26:00] Maya: okay good. Are there any blockers to enabling these changes immediately?

[26:20] Diego: no major blockers; the SSO fix needs your updated metadata. The retention change is a config flip. SOC2 package is paperwork and NDA.

[26:45] Samir: i'll upload the corrected metadata to the Jira ticket after this call.

[27:05] Laura: thanks. Could you also confirm backup retention for exported logs? Auditors want a 7-year archive for certain event categories.

[27:30] Diego: our standard export pipeline can push to your long-term storage (S3 Glacier). We'll propose a lifecycle policy and cost estimate.

[28:05] Maya: perfect. That should cover most of it.

[28:40] Priya: to summarize next steps quickly — SOC2 summary from Avery, log retention change from Diego, SSO test from Samir, deep dive Thurs 10:00 UTC. Any additions?

[29:10] Owen: just make sure the benchmark sheet ties to model + quantization and p95 numbers.

[29:28] Diego: will do.

[29:50] Maya: ok thanks everyone, appreciate the follow-through.

[30:10] Avery: thanks all, we'll circulate notes and action items. Meeting end.

(near the end there is some crosstalk and a dropped sentence: "...we'll push the config, uh, and then -")

End transcript.
